heating_mode_changed.text: get a notification when someone changes the mode on the control panel.
flow: WHEN Heating mode changed
THEN Send a push notification "Mode is now [Heating mode]"

water_mode_changed.text: this is an installation setting that normally does not change; create a notification when it does.
flow: WHEN Water mode changed
THEN Create a notification "Water mode changed to [Water mode]"

work_mode_changed.text: keep track of when Boost switches on.
flow: WHEN Work mode changed
AND Work mode is Boost
THEN Send a push notification "Boost is on"

capacity_setting_is.text: switch the hot water curve back on in the evening if it is off.
flow: WHEN The time is 22:00
AND Hot water curve setting is OFF
THEN Set hot water curve setting to H2

compressor_running.text: get a notification if the compressor is still running when an expensive period starts.
flow: WHEN Expensive period approaching
AND Compressor is running
THEN Send a push notification "The heat pump runs in the expensive period"

device_power_is.text: only lower the setpoint when the heat pump is on.
flow: WHEN The last person leaves
AND Device power is On
THEN Set target (setpoint) temperature to 30

dhw_heating_active.text: only switch on silent mode once the heat pump is no longer heating hot water.
flow: WHEN The time is 22:00
AND Hot water is not being heated
THEN Set silent mode to Level 2

heating_curve_is.text: only change the setpoint when the heating curve is OFF; with a heating curve the heat pump sets the supply temperature itself and does not keep a setpoint you set.
flow: WHEN The time is 06:00
AND Heating curve setting is OFF
THEN Set target (setpoint) temperature to 40

heating_mode_is.text: switch to hot water only in May, but only if the heat pump is still on heating and hot water. The Aurora III has other modes (Cooling, Heating, Auto) and no separate hot water mode.
flow: WHEN The time is 08:00
AND The day and month are 1 May
AND Heating mode is Heating and hot water
THEN Set heating mode to Hot water

hotwater_temperature_is.text: the card compares the hot water setpoint, not the measured tank temperature. Set the setpoint back if it stayed too high after a boost.
flow: WHEN The time is 23:00
AND Hot water temperature is Greater than 50°C
THEN Set hot water temperature to 48

silent_mode_is.text: switch silent mode off in the morning if it is still on.
flow: WHEN The time is 07:00
AND Silent mode is not Off
THEN Set silent mode to Off

target_temperature_is.text: only lower the setpoint at night if it is higher than the night value.
flow: WHEN The time is 23:00
AND Target (setpoint) temperature is Greater than 35°C
THEN Set target (setpoint) temperature to 32

volume_setting_is.text: this setting tells which power module the heat pump has (0 = none, 1 = single-phase, 2 = three-phase). Use the card to check that the value is still right, for example after a fault.
flow: WHEN The time is 08:00
AND Electricity consumption checking is not Equal to 1
THEN Send a push notification "Power module setting has changed"

water_mode_is.text: this is an installation setting; use the card to report an unexpected value.
flow: WHEN The time is 08:00
AND Water control mode is not Equal to 0
THEN Send a push notification "Water control mode is 1"

work_mode_is.text: set the heat pump back to Normal in the morning if it is still on ECO.
flow: WHEN The time is 07:00
AND Work mode is ECO
THEN Set work mode to Normal

set_backup_heater.text: force the electric backup heater in severe frost and release it when it is less cold.
flow: WHEN Ambient temperature changed below -10°C
THEN Switch forced backup heater on
WHEN Ambient temperature changed above -5°C
THEN Switch forced backup heater off

set_capacity.text: a higher hot water curve in the morning for the shower peak.
flow: WHEN The time is 05:30
THEN Set hot water curve setting to H3
WHEN The time is 09:00
THEN Set hot water curve setting to H1

set_curve_for_mode.text: set the floor heating curve at the start of the heating season.
flow: WHEN The time is 08:00
AND The day and month are 1 October
THEN Set curve to L3 for Floor heating

set_device_onoff.text: switch the heat pump on and off with a virtual button.
flow: WHEN Virtual button Heat pump is turned off
THEN Set device power to Off

set_dhw_function.text: switch hot water heating off during the holidays, with a Yes/No variable Holiday.
flow: WHEN A variable has changed (Holiday)
AND Holiday is equal to yes
THEN Switch hot water function off

set_diy_heating_curve.text: set a custom heating curve at the start of the heating season. The card also switches the custom curve on; a slope of -0.5 and 50 °C at -15 °C outside gives 40 °C supply at 5 °C outside.
flow: WHEN The time is 08:00
AND The day and month are 1 October
THEN Set Custom heating curve: slope -0.5, intercept 50°C

set_heating_curve.text: a higher heating curve from the start of the heating season.
flow: WHEN The time is 08:00
AND The day and month are 1 October
THEN Set heating curve setting to H4

set_heating_mode.text: switch back to heating and hot water at the start of the heating season. On the Aurora III choose Heating here.
flow: WHEN The time is 08:00
AND The day and month are 1 October
THEN Set heating mode to Heating and hot water

set_hotwater_temperature.text: heat the hot water extra in the cheapest block.
flow: WHEN Cheapest block started
THEN Set hot water temperature to 55
WHEN Expensive period approaching
THEN Set hot water temperature to 48

set_setpoint_for_mode.text: a lower floor heating setpoint at night. The setpoint only stays if the heating curve is OFF.
flow: WHEN The time is 23:00
THEN Set setpoint to 30 for Floor heating
Auto-round (recommended)
WHEN The time is 22:00
THEN Set silent mode to Level 2
WHEN The time is 07:00
THEN Set silent mode to Off

set_target_temperature.text: this is how you apply the recommendation of adaptive control: the control does not set the setpoint itself but gives a recommendation that your flow carries out. On the Aurora I/II the setpoint only stays if the heating curve is OFF. Do not also set the setpoint from another flow, or the two work against each other.
flow: WHEN Adaptive control recommends temperature adjustment
THEN Set target (setpoint) temperature to [Recommended target temperature]
Auto-round (recommended)

set_volume.text: this setting tells which power module the heat pump has (0 = none, 1 = single-phase, 2 = three-phase). Only change it when the installer says so; do not use the card in an automatic flow.

set_water_mode.text: this is an installation setting. Only change it when the installer says so; do not use the card in an automatic flow.

set_work_mode.text: Boost in the cheapest block, ECO in the expensive period.
flow: WHEN Cheapest block started
THEN Set work mode to Boost
WHEN Expensive period approaching
THEN Set work mode to ECO

ambient_temperature_changed.text: switch a virtual switch Heating season off when it gets warm outside. A switch that is already off stays off, so repeats do no harm.
flow: WHEN Ambient temperature changed above 18°C
THEN Turn Heating season off (virtual switch)

coiler_temperature_alert.text: record when the outdoor coil gets very cold, to help look for icing.
flow: WHEN Coiler temperature below -15°C
THEN Create a notification "[Current Coiler temperature] °C"

compressor_efficiency_alert.text: record when the compressor runs at high speed. The Tuya version needs the Expert cards setting switched on.
flow: WHEN Compressor frequency above 90 Hz
THEN Create a notification "Compressor at [Current frequency] Hz"

discharge_temperature_alert.text: send a notification when the compressor gets too hot.
flow: WHEN Discharge temperature above 105°C
THEN Send a push notification "Discharge above 105 °C, check the heat pump"

economizer_inlet_temperature_alert.text: follow the economizer (EVI heat exchanger) when looking for a fault.
flow: WHEN Economizer inlet temperature below -10°C
THEN Create a notification "[Current Economizer inlet temperature] °C"

economizer_outlet_temperature_alert.text: follow the economizer (EVI heat exchanger) when looking for a fault.
flow: WHEN Economizer outlet temperature above 60°C
THEN Create a notification "[Current Economizer outlet temperature] °C"

eev_pulse_steps_alert.text: record when the expansion valve closes far, to help look for a fault.
flow: WHEN EEV pulse-steps below 50
THEN Create a notification "EEV [Current EEV Open pulse-steps]"

evi_pulse_steps_alert.text: record how far the EVI valve opens, to help look for a fault.
flow: WHEN EVI Open pulse-steps above 300
THEN Create a notification "EVI [Current EVI Open pulse-steps]"

fan_motor_efficiency_alert.text: record when the fan runs at high speed. The Tuya version needs the Expert cards setting switched on.
flow: WHEN Fan motor frequency above 60 Hz
THEN Create a notification "Fan at [Current fan frequency] Hz"

fault_detected.text: get a notification for a specific fault. On the Modbus drivers the code is text as on the display (for example F1.1 or E03), on Tuya a number. For every fault at once, use the condition Fault is active.
flow: WHEN Fault F1.1 detected
THEN Send a push notification "Fault [Fault code]: [Fault description]"

high_pressure_temperature_alert.text: record when the high-pressure side gets very warm.
flow: WHEN High pressure temperature above 55°C
THEN Create a notification "[Current High pressure temperature] °C"

incoiler_temperature_alert.text: record when the condenser gets very warm.
flow: WHEN Incoiler temperature above 60°C
THEN Create a notification "Condenser [Current Incoiler temperature] °C"

inlet_temperature_changed.text: switch a virtual switch Return warm on once the return water is warm enough.
flow: WHEN Inlet temperature changed above 30°C
THEN Turn Return warm on (virtual switch)

inlet_temperature_value_changed.text: keep the return temperature in a number variable, for example for another flow. The card fires on every change of at least 0.5 °C.
flow: WHEN Inlet temperature has changed
THEN Set a number variable: Return to [Current inlet temperature]

low_pressure_temperature_alert.text: record when the low-pressure side gets very cold.
flow: WHEN Low pressure temperature below -20°C
THEN Create a notification "[Current Low pressure temperature] °C"

outlet_temperature_changed.text: warn when the supply gets too warm for floor heating. The card fires again on every further rise of 0.5 °C.
flow: WHEN Outlet temperature changed above 45°C
AND Heating mode is Floor heating
THEN Send a push notification "Supply [Current outlet temperature] °C"

outlet_temperature_value_changed.text: keep the supply temperature in a number variable. The card fires on every change of at least 0.5 °C.
flow: WHEN Outlet temperature has changed
THEN Set a number variable: Supply to [Current outlet temperature]

suction_temperature_alert.text: record when the suction gas gets very cold.
flow: WHEN Suction temperature below -20°C
THEN Create a notification "Suction [Current Suction temperature] °C"

tank_temperature_alert.text: show with a virtual switch whether the tank is warm.
flow: WHEN Tank temperature above 50°C
THEN Turn Tank warm on (virtual switch)
WHEN Tank temperature below 40°C
THEN Turn Tank warm off

water_flow_alert.text: one notification for too little flow, with a Yes/No variable Flow alert against repeats. The Tuya version needs the Expert cards setting switched on.
flow: WHEN Water flow rate below 10 L/min
AND Compressor is running
AND Flow alert is equal to no
THEN Send a push notification "Low flow: [Current flow rate] L/min"
AND Set a Yes/No variable: Flow alert to yes
WHEN Water flow rate above 15 L/min
THEN Set a Yes/No variable: Flow alert to no

electrical_balance_check.text: check daily whether the three phases carry about the same load.
flow: WHEN The time is 12:00
AND Compressor is running
AND 3-phase electrical balance is outside 10% tolerance
THEN Send a push notification "Phases unevenly loaded"

fault_active.text: get a reminder every morning as long as a fault is still active.
flow: WHEN The time is 08:00
AND Fault is active
THEN Send a push notification "The heat pump still reports a fault"

system_pulse_steps_differential.text: record the difference between the EEV and EVI valves, to help look for a fault.
flow: WHEN The time is 14:00
AND System pulse-steps differential is above 300
THEN Create a notification "Large difference EEV and EVI"

temperature_above.text: heat the hot water extra in the cheapest block, but only when it is cold outside.
flow: WHEN Cheapest block started
AND Ambient temperature is below 5°C
THEN Set hot water temperature to 55
AND Set hot water temperature to 48 (delay 4 hours)

temperature_differential.text: a large difference between supply and return can point to too little flow.
flow: WHEN The time is 14:00
AND Compressor is running
AND Temperature differential is above 8°C
THEN Send a push notification "Large difference supply and return"

water_flow_rate_check.text: check the flow at a fixed time while the compressor runs.
flow: WHEN The time is 10:00
AND Compressor is running
AND Water flow rate is below 15 L/min
THEN Send a push notification "Low flow, check the filter"

cop_efficiency_changed.text: record a low COP, with the calculation method used. The card looks at every change of at least 0.3.
flow: WHEN COP efficiency changed below 2
AND Compressor is running
THEN Create a notification "COP [Current COP] ([Calculation method used])"

cop_outlier_detected.text: an outlier often points to a sensor that is wrong or a missing power measurement; record it in the timeline.
flow: WHEN COP outlier detected
THEN Create a notification "COP [Outlier COP value]: [Outlier reason]"

cop_trend_detected.text: get a notification when efficiency clearly declines over the last 24 hours.
flow: WHEN COP trend detected: degrading
THEN Send a push notification "[Trend description]"

daily_consumption_threshold.text: get one notification a day once consumption reaches a limit.
flow: WHEN Daily consumption reached 30 kWh
THEN Send a push notification "Already [Daily consumption] kWh today"

daily_cop_efficiency_changed.text: record when the daily COP drops below a limit. The card looks at every change of at least 0.2.
flow: WHEN Daily COP efficiency changed below 3
THEN Create a notification "Daily COP [Current daily COP]"

daily_cost_threshold.text: get one notification a day when energy costs exceed an amount. Only works with price optimization and an external energy measurement.
flow: WHEN Daily cost exceeded €5
THEN Send a push notification "Cost today € [Today's Total Cost (€)]"

monthly_cop_efficiency_changed.text: follow efficiency over 30 days. The card looks at every change of at least 0.2.
flow: WHEN Monthly COP efficiency changed below 3
THEN Send a push notification "Monthly COP [Current monthly COP]"

performance_report_ready.text: receive a short summary every evening at 23:00.
flow: WHEN Performance report is ready
THEN Send a push notification "[Rating]: [Summary]"

power_threshold_exceeded.text: record when the heat pump draws a lot of power. The card fires once when the threshold is crossed and again only after the power has dropped first. Requires a power measurement.
flow: WHEN Power consumption exceeded 3000 W
THEN Create a notification "Power [Current power consumption] W"

total_consumption_milestone.text: a reminder at a consumption milestone, for example for maintenance.
flow: WHEN Total consumption reached 10000 kWh
THEN Send a push notification "[Total consumption] kWh: plan maintenance"

cop_calculation_method_is.text: only react to a low COP when it was calculated from measured flow, temperatures and power.
flow: WHEN COP efficiency changed below 2
AND COP calculation method is Direct thermal (most accurate)
THEN Send a push notification "Low COP: [Current COP]"

cop_efficiency_check.text: heat the hot water extra in the afternoon when the heat pump runs efficiently at that moment, and set the setpoint back in the evening.
flow: WHEN The time is 14:00
AND COP efficiency is above 4
THEN Set hot water temperature to 55
WHEN The time is 18:00
THEN Set hot water temperature to 48
WHEN The time is 10:00
AND Today is a Sunday
AND COP trend is degrading over 168 hours
THEN Send a push notification "Efficiency is declining this week"

daily_cop_above_threshold.text: add a warning to the evening report when the daily COP was low.
flow: WHEN Performance report is ready
AND Daily COP is below 2.5
THEN Send a push notification "Low daily COP: [Summary]"

monthly_cop_above_threshold.text: record when the monthly COP is below a limit.
flow: WHEN Performance report is ready
AND Monthly COP is below 3
THEN Create a notification "Monthly COP below 3"

power_above_threshold.text: set the heat pump to ECO when it draws a lot of power in the expensive period. Requires a power measurement; the Aurora III has no ECO mode.
flow: WHEN Expensive period approaching
AND Power consumption is above 1500 watts
THEN Set work mode to ECO

total_consumption_above.text: a yearly reminder once total consumption has passed a limit.
flow: WHEN The time is 08:00
AND The day and month are 1 September
AND Total consumption is above 20000 kWh
THEN Send a push notification "Time for maintenance"

generate_performance_report.text: create the report at another time than 23:00 and pass on the result.
flow: WHEN The time is 18:00
AND Today is a Sunday
THEN Generate performance report
AND Send a push notification "[Rating]: [Summary]"

cheapest_block_started.text: heat the hot water extra in the cheapest block and set it back afterwards, with a delay on the second action card. The block length is set in Price Block Size (hours), default 4. Only works when adaptive control is running (with an indoor temperature), price optimization is on, and prices come in through Send external energy prices.
flow: WHEN Cheapest block started
THEN Set hot water temperature to 55
AND Set hot water temperature to 48 (delay 4 hours)

expensive_block_approaching.text: set the heat pump to ECO before the expensive period starts. How many hours ahead the card fires is set in Expensive Block Warning Time (hours), default 2. The Aurora III has no ECO. Only works when adaptive control is running (with an indoor temperature), price optimization is on, and prices come in through Send external energy prices.
flow: WHEN Expensive period approaching
THEN Set work mode to ECO
AND Send a push notification "Expensive from [Block Start Time]"

price_threshold_crossed.text: ECO at a very high price and back to Normal at any other category. The category is a code: very_low, low, normal, high or very_high. Only works when adaptive control is running (with an indoor temperature), price optimization is on, and prices come in through Send external energy prices.
flow: WHEN Energy price crossed threshold
AND [Price Category] is exactly very_high
THEN Set work mode to ECO
ELSE Set work mode to Normal

price_trend_changed.text: create a notification when prices start rising or falling. Only works when adaptive control is running (with an indoor temperature), price optimization is on, and prices come in through Send external energy prices.
flow: WHEN Price trend changed
THEN Create a notification "Price trend [Previous Trend] to [New Trend]"

price_in_cheapest_hours.text: only heat the hot water in the three cheapest hours of the day. Requires prices through Send external energy prices.
flow: WHEN Every 1 hour
AND Current hour is in cheapest 3 hours of today
THEN Set hot water temperature to 55
ELSE Set hot water temperature to 48

price_trend_is.text: heat the hot water in the morning when prices rise in the coming hours, and set it back later. Requires prices through Send external energy prices.
flow: WHEN The time is 06:00
AND Price trend for next 6 hours is Rising
THEN Set hot water temperature to 55
AND Set hot water temperature to 48 (delay 3 hours)

price_vs_daily_average.text: Boost when the price is well below the daily average, otherwise Normal. Requires prices through Send external energy prices; the Aurora III has no Boost.
flow: WHEN Every 1 hour
AND Current price is below daily average by 20%
THEN Set work mode to Boost
ELSE Set work mode to Normal

savings_above.text: since version 3.4.2 the app no longer estimates a saving in euros, because it cannot be substantiated with dynamic prices. The card always returns false. Use Insight is active instead.

receive_external_energy_prices.text: the app does not fetch prices itself. Send them as text from another app, a variable or an HTTP request, for example [0.21,0.19,0.18,...] in €/kWh, where the first number is the current hour. The prices apply from the moment they are received; send new ones when they are available, for example every afternoon after tomorrow's prices are published.
flow: WHEN The time is 14:30
THEN Send external energy prices [Prices] for price optimization

temperature_adjustment_recommended.text: this is the core of adaptive control: the control does not set the setpoint itself, this flow carries out the recommendation. On the Aurora I/II via Modbus the recommendation follows the mode; use Set setpoint temperature (by mode) on Auto there. On the Aurora I/II the setpoint only stays if the heating curve is OFF.
flow: WHEN Adaptive control recommends temperature adjustment
THEN Set target (setpoint) temperature to [Recommended target temperature]
Auto-round (recommended)

adaptive_simulation_update.text: the card fires every control cycle (about every 5 minutes). Use it to keep track of values, not for notifications.
flow: WHEN Simulated target temperature updated
THEN Set a number variable: Advice to [Simulated Target (°C)]

adaptive_status_change.text: get a notification when adaptive control switches on or off.
flow: WHEN Adaptive control status changed
THEN Send a push notification "Adaptive control [Status]: [Reason]"

building_insight_detected.text: receive a new insight about the house as soon as the building model is reliable enough (setting Minimum Confidence (%), default 70%).
flow: WHEN New building insight detected
THEN Send a push notification "[Insight] [Recommendation]"

building_profile_mismatch.text: the learned behaviour does not match the chosen building type. Choose the suggested type in the settings (Building Type) to learn faster.
flow: WHEN Building profile mismatch detected
THEN Send a push notification "Building type [Suggested Profile] fits better"

forecast_heating_advice.text: receive the advice based on the expected outdoor temperature: wait because it gets warmer and so more efficient later, or heat now. The card fires when the advice changes. Requires the weather forecast in the settings. The advice text is currently always in Dutch.
flow: WHEN Forecast heating advice available
THEN Create a notification "[Advice]"

learning_milestone_reached.text: get one notification when the building model reaches 70% confidence. After learning starts over, the card fires again.
flow: WHEN Building model learning milestone
THEN Send a push notification "Building model: [Milestone]"

pre_heat_recommendation.text: the card fires when it is more than 1.5 °C colder than desired and the building model is reliable enough (setting Minimum Confidence (%), default 70%), at most once every 4 hours.
flow: WHEN Pre-heating time recommendation
THEN Send a push notification "Warming up takes [Duration (hours)] hours"

confidence_above.text: only carry out the recommendation when the building model is reliable enough.
flow: WHEN Adaptive control recommends temperature adjustment
AND Model confidence is above 70%
THEN Set target (setpoint) temperature to [Recommended target temperature]
Auto-round (recommended)

insight_is_active.text: a weekly reminder of an open insight.
flow: WHEN The time is 09:00
AND Today is a Monday
AND Insulation performance insight is active
THEN Send a push notification "There is an insight about the insulation"

calculate_preheat_time.text: calculate at night when heating has to start to reach 21 °C at 07:00. Enter the time as HH:MM.
flow: WHEN The time is 04:00
THEN Calculate when to start heating to reach 21°C at 07:00
AND Send a push notification "Start at [Start time]"

force_insight_analysis.text: update the insights right away instead of waiting for the next analysis (every 50 minutes).
flow: WHEN The time is 08:00
THEN Force insight analysis
AND Create a notification "[Insights detected] insights"

set_desired_indoor_temperature.text: a lower desired indoor temperature at night. Adaptive control adjusts its recommendation to it.
flow: WHEN The time is 22:30
THEN Set desired indoor temperature to 19°C
WHEN The time is 06:30
THEN Set desired indoor temperature to 21°C

receive_external_indoor_temperature.text: adaptive control only works with an indoor temperature. Send it on every change of a room sensor, preferably with the sensor's token. If the value stays the same for 12 hours the app reports it; after 24 hours the control no longer corrects on it. If you type a value yourself, use a point (21.5).
flow: WHEN The temperature has changed (living room sensor)
THEN Send [Temperature]°C indoor temperature for adaptive control

receive_external_ambient_data.text: use your own outdoor sensor instead of the heat pump's sensor. A value counts for an hour; after that adaptive control falls back to the weather forecast and the heat pump's sensor.
flow: WHEN The temperature has changed (outdoor sensor)
THEN Send [Temperature]°C to heat pump for COP/thermal mass calculation

receive_external_power_data.text: send the measured power of a kWh meter or smart plug, also when it drops to 0 W. This gives the most accurate COP calculation and fills daily consumption and daily cost. For the COP a value counts for an hour; daily consumption keeps counting with the last value received.
flow: WHEN The power has changed (heat pump kWh meter)
THEN Send [Power]W to heat pump for COP calculation

receive_external_flow_data.text: send the flow of an external flow meter, if the heat pump does not measure it itself. A value counts for an hour.
flow: WHEN (trigger of your flow meter on a new reading)
THEN Send [Flow]L/min to heat pump for COP calculation

receive_external_solar_power.text: the app converts the power of the solar panels into solar radiation for the building model. Fill in Solar panel system size (Wp) in the settings for this. A value counts for an hour; after that the app falls back to the weather forecast.
flow: WHEN The power has changed (solar inverter)
THEN Send solar power [Power]W to heat pump

receive_external_solar_radiation.text: send the measured solar radiation, for example from a weather app. Solar panels take precedence if they also send data. A value counts for an hour.
flow: WHEN Every 15 minutes
THEN Send solar radiation [Solar radiation from your weather app] W/m²
to heat pump

receive_external_wind_data.text: send the wind speed for the heat loss correction. The card expects km/h; a value in m/s times 3.6 is km/h. A value counts for an hour; after that the app falls back to the weather forecast.
flow: WHEN Every 15 minutes
THEN Send wind speed [Wind speed from your weather app] km/h to heat pump

calculate_curve_value.text: make your own heating curve in steps: the first rule that matches decides the result. On the Aurora I/II the setpoint only stays if the heat pump's heating curve is OFF; do not use this together with adaptive control.
flow: WHEN Every 30 minutes
THEN Calculate value via [Ambient temperature of the heat pump]
using curve rules < 0 : 55, < 5 : 50, < 10 : 45, default : 35
AND Set target (setpoint) temperature to [Result Value]
Auto-round (recommended)

calculate_linear_heating_curve.text: calculate the supply temperature of a straight heating curve like the heat pump's custom curve: L29 is the supply at -15 °C outside, L28 the slope per 10 °C. With 55 and -5, 5 °C outside gives 45 °C supply. Useful to try out a curve first.
flow: WHEN Every 30 minutes
THEN Calculate heating curve: L29=55°C at -15°C, L28=-5/10°C
with outdoor temp [Ambient temperature of the heat pump]
AND Create a notification "Curve gives [Supply Temperature] °C"

calculate_time_based_value.text: a daily schedule for the desired indoor temperature. Periods across midnight are allowed; default : value catches the rest.
flow: WHEN Every 30 minutes
THEN Calculate value from time periods
AND Set desired indoor temperature to [Result value]°C

get_seasonal_mode.text: the heating season runs from 1 October to 15 May. Store the result in a Yes/No variable, so other flows can test it.
flow: WHEN The time is 00:05
THEN Get seasonal mode
AND Set a Yes/No variable: Heating season to [Is heating season]

modbus_read_register.text: read a register the app does not show. On the Aurora I/II the address is hex or decimal (0x0301 = 769, the heating setpoint); temperatures are stored ×10. On the Aurora III use the number after 4- (4-2100 becomes 2100); input registers (3-) cannot be read with this card.
flow: WHEN The time is 12:00
THEN Read Modbus register 0x0301
AND Create a notification "Register 0x0301: [Register value]"

modbus_write_register.text: only write to a register when you know what it does; a wrong value can upset the heat pump. Temperatures are ×10: 350 is 35 °C. On the Aurora I/II the heating setpoint (0x0301) only stays if the heating curve is OFF.
flow: WHEN The time is 06:00
THEN Write 350 to Modbus register 0x0301
